headline: Midwest flooding expands into Nebraska as multi-day rainfall continues, while new wildfires erupt on Croatia's Brač Island and California's Big Sur coast.
overview: A persistent slow-moving storm system is driving a second day of excessive rainfall across a broad swath of Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, and Nebraska, with Flood Watches now extending through Wednesday and rivers approaching or above flood stage. Simultaneously, new wildfires have ignited on Croatia's Brač Island — forcing over 200 evacuations — and California's Big Sur coast, where two fires have collectively scorched nearly 60,000 acres. Geological and volcanic activity remains elevated globally, with Kīlauea continuing episodic fountaining in Hawaii, Indonesia's ongoing karhutla wildfire and haze crisis spanning 202,000+ hectares, and a recently recorded M6.5 earthquake off the northwest coast of Java.

events.title: Midwest Multi-State Flood Crisis Expands — Iowa, Kansas, Missouri & Nebraska
events.location: Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, and Nebraska, USA
events.summary: A second consecutive day of excessive rainfall is battering a broad multi-state corridor, with NWS Flood Watches now active across dozens of counties in Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, and Nebraska through at least Wednesday afternoon. Localized totals of 3–5 inches are possible on top of already-saturated soils, threatening rivers including the Raccoon, Missouri, and Kansas to approach or overtop flood stage. The Raccoon River at Des Moines Fleur Drive is under a specific Flood Watch through Tuesday night, and the Kansas City metro area faces escalating river flooding risk through mid-week.

articles.title: Iowa Weather: Heavy Rain Sunday, Severe Storm Risk Monday

events.title: Big Sur Wildfires — Timber & Plaskett Fires Near 60,000 Acres Combined
events.location: Big Sur, Monterey and San Luis Obispo Counties, California, USA
events.summary: Two large wildfires burning near Big Sur on the California Central Coast have collectively scorched nearly 60,000 acres, with the Timber Fire — now approximately one month old — and the Plaskett Fire (ignited August 26) together posing ongoing threats to the rugged coastal region. Evacuation orders and warnings remain active across portions of Monterey County, though growth on both fires has slowed and Highway 1 closures have been partially reduced as containment improves. The fires are burning in steep, inaccessible terrain that has complicated aerial and ground suppression efforts.

articles.title: One month after start of Timber Fire, progress made in fighting Big Sur wildfires
Hwy. 1 closure reduces as Big Sur fire containment improves

events.title: Brač Island Wildfire — 200+ Evacuated on Croatia's Largest Adriatic Island
events.summary: A major wildfire erupted on Brač, Croatia's largest Adriatic island, forcing the evacuation of more than 200 residents and tourists beginning around September 12–13 and continuing to burn as of September 14. Croatian firefighting crews have been deployed near the town of Milna, and the EU Space Agency confirmed visible scarring of the island in satellite imagery. The fire adds to the wider Western Balkans wildfire crisis that has already been burning across Bosnia, Montenegro, Albania, and Serbia this week.

articles.title: Wildfire Map Spotlight: Brac Island Fire, Croatia

events.title: Kīlauea Summit Eruption — Episodic Fountaining Continues, USGS WATCH Maintained
events.location: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park, Big Island, Hawaii, USA
events.summary: Kīlauea's summit eruption within Kaluapele caldera continues to produce episodic lava fountaining, incandescence, and intermittent spatter, with the USGS maintaining its WATCH alert level as of September 13. Lava has periodically overflowed crater margins in prior episodes, and activity remains dynamic with precursory low-level lava movement observed in overnight webcam imagery. The eruption poses no immediate threat to populated areas but continues to draw significant scientific and public attention.

events.title: Indonesia Karhutla Crisis — 202,000+ Hectares Burned, Transboundary Haze Persists
events.summary: Indonesia's karhutla (forest and land fire) season remains in full crisis as of September 13, with widespread surface and peat fires burning across Sumatra and Kalimantan having scorched more than 202,000 hectares in 2026. Thick transboundary haze continues to degrade air quality across neighboring Southeast Asian nations, a recurring and severe public health emergency. The combination of drought-dried peatlands and agricultural burning is driving the crisis, which shows no immediate sign of abatement.

events.title: M6.5 Deep Earthquake — Northwest Java, Indonesia
events.location: 126 km NNE of Teluknaga, Java, Indonesia
events.summary: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck approximately 126 km north-northeast of Teluknaga on the northwest coast of Java on September 11 at 21:23 UTC, according to USGS data. The event occurred at a depth of 372 km — deep enough to significantly attenuate surface shaking — and was assigned a green USGS alert level with no tsunami alert issued; 21 felt reports were recorded. The Watchers reported the event as an M6.6, suggesting slight magnitude revision, with the epicenter located roughly 115 km north of the Java coast.

articles.title: Strong M6.6 earthquake hits Java, Indonesia

events.title: Fairbanks, Alaska Flood Watch — Chena River at Bankfull Through Saturday
events.location: Fairbanks Metro Area and Upper Kuskokwim Valley, Alaska, USA
events.summary: The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued Flood Watches through Friday–Saturday for the Fairbanks metro area and Upper Kuskokwim Valley, citing the Chena River currently running at or near bankfull with soils saturated from persistent heavy rainfall. Additional rainfall through the week threatens to push the Chena and Little Chena rivers over their banks, potentially affecting Fairbanks, North Pole, Two Rivers, Fort Wainwright, and surrounding communities. Late-season Arctic flooding events of this duration and areal extent are relatively uncommon and warrant close monitoring.
